subject: Stakeholder mapping & procurement path for Redwood evaluation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@orionhealth.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orionhealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Stakeholder mapping & procurement path for Redwood evaluation

Hi Sofia and Liam,

Thanks again for taking the time today 



appreciated the candid overview of the use case and the key latency/cost objectives for your virtual triage assistants. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our side: 

- Summary: Correct me if I missed anything, but primary goal is to reduce avg response time from 1.6s to <1.0s for patient triage flows while keeping monthly inference spend within the pilot budget.
- Pilot scope: 6-week pilot with a sandbox dataset and SOC2-compliant access (no PHI in the initial run).
- Key decision criteria you mentioned: latency, predictable unit cost, and clear audit logs for regulatory review.

Next steps we discussed:
1) Share a stakeholder map / org chart and indicate the economic buyer + procurement/security contacts.
2) Procurement/security checklist so we can prepare SOC2 and access controls documentation in parallel.
3) Redwood will provide a short SOW + sample pricing for the pilot. Attached are the call notes and a quick stakeholder mapping template to make the ask easier.

Attachments: call_notes.pdf (summary), redwood-stakeholder-template.xlsx

Would you be able to share the org chart and procurement contact by end of week? If it helps, Rishi from our team can coordinate a short intro with Procurement & Security to speed approvals.

Thanks 

Marissa

Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Perfect 


thanks Liam. A couple of requests to make the intros as productive as possible:

- Could you flag the economic buyer (title and name) so we can tailor the pilot economics to their evaluation metrics?
- For Security: if you can share the top 3 evidence items they'll want (e.g., SOC 2 report, encryption at rest details, data retention policy), Neha can prepare those ahead of the intro.
- For Procurement: sample contract terms you typically require (preferred invoicing cadence, PO requirements, any insurance limits) help us avoid rework.

I'm attaching a short stakeholder-template (redwood-stakeholder-template.xlsx) that shows the fields we find helpful (role, influence, decision timing). I've also dropped a drive link below if you prefer to upload org materials there.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-link

If Thursday works for you, Rishi and I can be on the procurement/security intro early next week.

Thanks again,
Marissa

attaching our org chart (orion_orgchart_v2.pdf) and a quick list of key stakeholders below:

- Anjali Rao 
— VP of Clinical Ops (economic buyer; final approval)

— Head of Platform Engineering (technical evaluation)
- Priya Singh

— Security Lead (security & compliance owner; security@orionhealth.com)

Let me know if you want to set a joint sync with Anjali and procurement next week
